steps.content: The late-night office is silent with only the gentle hum of the air conditioner, a sharp contrast to the piercing male voice on the other end of the call.
I've been calling for half an hour. Glad you're finally free to pick up the phone.
You glance at the two-digit number following the caller ID, mustering the energy to switch to your most polite voice.

steps.speaker: Chief
steps.content: Excuse me, may I know if you're Shrooma's...?

steps.speaker: Chief
steps.content: I've already explained the situation to Shrooma's aunt, second aunt-in-law, and third cousin when they called before.

steps.speaker: Chief
steps.content: We're at a crucial stage of the summer camp and we strongly advise against taking her away unless it's absolutely necessary, as this would cause her to fall behind her classmates...
Cut it out if you're just going to repeat the same thing!
The man's voice interrupts you vehemently, as if your rehearsed sentences have kindled his pent-up anger.
Like we've emphasized repeatedly, the banquet in two days is of utmost importance to our family. We need Shrooma to be there despite any situation!
She's our golden girl who's never made a mistake. She will serve her family when need be. When we called before, didn't you praise her a lot too?
In that case, why would you stop her from leaving the camp for just one night?!
As her guardians, we have every right to suspect that something's gone wrong under your supervision! Your every move is a deliberate cover-up!
Despite any situation, "golden girl," "serve her family"... His anger sounds genuine, which only makes you more helpless.
It's hard to imagine these words being used on a schoolgirl and worse still, turned by her guardians into an unavoidable curse against you, the "instructor."

steps.speaker: Chief
steps.content: Our summer camp is compliant with all the regulations, please do not worry. That being said... I hear what you're saying.

steps.speaker: Chief
steps.content: If the guardians insist, we will review Shrooma's leave request and provide you with a definite answer the soonest we can.
It was wise to back down. After getting a satisfactory answer, the man immediately ends the call. His purpose can't be made clearer.
Before you can catch your breath, the ever-efficient Adjutant Nightingale brings you the important file you're waiting for. A folder containing the necessary documents to bail Shrooma out.

steps.speaker: Nightingale
steps.content: According to the documents, Sinner Shrooma's psychological evaluation, supervision records, and special power assessment have all passed review, but she firmly refuses to sign the bail form.
The blank form speaks for the girl's decision. You can't help but pinch your nose bridge.

steps.speaker: Chief
steps.content: Her guardians are equally adamant about her attending the so-called banquet and won't stop pressuring us. We must find a way to untangle this deadlock...

steps.speaker: Nightingale
steps.content: Considering her situation, her bail request will no doubt be accepted. Chief, why don't you open up to her guardians about the truth of the "summer camp" and tell them what she thinks?

steps.speaker: Chief
steps.content: We still don't know why she refuse bail. Maybe she simply doesn't want to go home. Doing so would mean shifting the pressure onto Shrooma.

steps.speaker: Chief
steps.content: Let's arrange for an interrogation tomorrow. I think we need to have an in-depth talk with our little Sinner.

steps.speaker: Shrooma
steps.content: Greetings, Chief.
The girl in the interrogation chair sits upright, her hands placed neatly on her knees, good upbringing reflected even in her perfect smile.

steps.speaker: Chief
steps.content: Morning, Shrooma.

steps.speaker: Chief
steps.content: How are you finding life in the Bureau? Everything good?

steps.speaker: Shrooma
steps.content: I'm a bit attached to my usual bed, so my sleep has been affected slightly. Other than that, everything's fine.

steps.speaker: Shrooma
steps.content: Everyone here doesn't fuss over me because of my age and I get along with them well. Adjutant Nightingale also takes good care of me.

steps.speaker: Shrooma
steps.content: Overall, I think I'm adapting pretty well. At least I feel much better than at school! After all, on campus, big shots like you will never personally check on me like this.
She answers honestly in a relaxed tone. As far as interrogations go, it's a good start.
But you sense that she's still wary of you. She can clearly tell you're not here just for small talk. Unfortunately, her hunch is right.

steps.speaker: Chief
steps.content: That's great to hear. I'm glad you're adjusting well to your new life and not feeling stressed from the change.

steps.speaker: Chief
steps.content: I've noticed you seem to be posting fewer rants on forums recently.

steps.speaker: Chief
steps.content: Is that why you refuse to be bailed out and go back to school and your family?
You gently tap the blank signature section of the bail form on the desk with your knuckle, inquiring about Shrooma's thoughts with a dull thud.

steps.speaker: Chief
steps.content: Is it because hiding here allows you to escape the overwhelming stress in your life, just like hiding behind a fake username on a forum?
The girl's pupils contract slightly, clearly taken aback by your bluntness. She bites her lip almost defensively.

steps.speaker: Chief
steps.content: Don't be afraid. I'm not here to lecture you today. I just want to know what concerns you about the bail.

steps.speaker: Chief
steps.content: We understand that the current pre-bail assessment may not be enough. If you feel that your family and social circles can't provide you enough support to return as a Sinner...

steps.speaker: Chief
steps.content: The Bureau will not force you to go back.
A long silence. When Shrooma speaks again, her honesty becomes more genuine, yet also more aggressive, much like the voices on the other end of those phone calls.

steps.speaker: Shrooma
steps.content: ...That sounds fair. But Chief, that's not why you brought me here today, is it?

steps.speaker: Shrooma
steps.content: You just want me to sign the bail form and get out of here, right?

steps.speaker: Shrooma
steps.content: My family have been pushing you, haven't they? Are they circling you like hungry pigeons begging for food, bothering you?

steps.speaker: Chief
steps.content: Shrooma, you're more mature than I imagined.
"Mature" was your first impression of her, but right now, what she displays surpasses that apt maturity and turns into wisdom that demands serious attention.

steps.speaker: Shrooma
steps.content: You can be honest with me. I'm not the little fool you think I am.

steps.speaker: Shrooma
steps.content: My family is so eager for me to show up... Is it some important social event within their circle? Some boring upper-class ball? Or is it that banquet?

steps.speaker: Shrooma
steps.content: Your face tells that I've guessed right. It's the banquet.

steps.speaker: Chief
steps.content: ...Are all these things you just mentioned already scheduled?

steps.speaker: Shrooma
steps.content: Of course, my schedule is always full.
She sneers with disdain.

steps.speaker: Shrooma
steps.content: You must know how the high society of Eastside views immigrants. They despise these upstarts, and are also wary of the foreigners.

steps.speaker: Shrooma
steps.content: My family is no exception. As mere immigrant merchants, we don't qualify for invitations to those elite banquets.

steps.speaker: Shrooma
steps.content: Only through "academic socializing" can my family scrape into these disgusting exchanges to pick up some leftovers.

steps.speaker: Shrooma
steps.content: The so-called pure, non-political socializing among family successors in their youthful school days.

steps.speaker: Shrooma
steps.content: In reality, it's just a hypocritical show they put their children through.

steps.speaker: Shrooma
steps.content: Show off your superb violin skills and upper-class etiquette... And show off your family's obedience and humility toward the rules!
The well-trained smile that Shrooma always wears has long disappeared.
Her habitual obedience is no doubt also just a "show"... Probably a social capital her family uses to exchange for benefit.

steps.speaker: Chief
steps.content: Is that why you refuse to sign the form and go home? Because you're tired of adults asking you to "put on a show"?

steps.speaker: Shrooma
steps.content: Of course!
Your words are free of contempt, but Shrooma still raises her voice as if triggered.

steps.speaker: Shrooma
steps.content: Those who barely made it into an elite school don't deserve to enjoy youth! Not only must I get good grades, but I also need to flatter my classmates!

steps.speaker: Shrooma
steps.content: Which means enduring every jerk's pranks and kissing those idiots' arse! Only then can I become the class president and get those invitations for my family!

steps.speaker: Shrooma
steps.content: Who would want that kind of life? I can't even breathe! Everywhere I go, I must keep that same smile and repeat "it's okay" again and again!
She growls out the words as her chest heaves slightly, her emotions finally peeking over the high walls built by so-called etiquette and discipline.
This reminds you of those anonymous posts she posted on forums, venting her hatred toward the arrogant classmates and snobbish teachers. You begin to understand her.
She must keep putting on a perfect show for her family's benefit and to spare them harm. The internet might be the only outlet for her emotions.
She's our golden girl who's never made a mistake. She will serve her family when need be.
But... rather than turning a blind eye to them, her family seem genuinely unaware of her suppressed disgust and emotions. They truly think she's "perfect." Why?

steps.speaker: Chief
steps.content: Do you never let down your disguise even in front of your family...? Are they dangerous to you too?

steps.speaker: Shrooma
steps.content: Huh? What? Are you saying that's what I should do, or that I shouldn't be too sensitive?!

steps.speaker: Chief
steps.content: No, I didn't mean that. It's just that your family is not as loving and caring as our initial assessment suggested, which is an oversight on our part.

steps.speaker: Chief
steps.content: Such an environment may not be accepting enough to accommodate a Sinner who could bring more risks than benefits.

steps.speaker: Shrooma
steps.content: You think so too, don't you? How could a family accept a Sinner if they can't even accept her "imperfections"?

steps.speaker: Chief
steps.content: Yes, I understand. In that case, agreeing to be bailed out and revealing your identity as a Sinner indeed bring more harm than good.

steps.speaker: Shrooma
steps.content: Exactly! Since you get it now, does that mean I can...!
Her eyes light up. Perhaps your empathy, sincerity, and courage to admit your mistakes have moved her.
But that's also why you can't brush her off with lies.

steps.speaker: Chief
steps.content: Hold on, let me finish. This is just a guess, and since your legal guardians are still alive, the Bureau has no legitimate reason to take over your guardianship.

steps.speaker: Chief
steps.content: Whether you get bailed out or not, the rules demand us to disclose your identity as a Sinner to your guardians sooner or later.

steps.speaker: Shrooma
steps.content: ...What if I never sign the bail?
Back to square one. Seeing Shrooma's childish attempt at passive resistance, you tentatively present the alternative you've prepared.

steps.speaker: Chief
steps.content: I understand your reluctance, but complete confidentiality is indeed unrealistic. There may be room for compromise...

steps.speaker: Chief
steps.content: For instance, can your parents or anyone in your family who can sign as your guardian help conceal the truth from the rest of your family?
The dimmed eyes, her silence, and those clenched fingers already answer your question.

steps.speaker: Chief
steps.content: Alright. In that case, we can come up with something else...
Before you finish speaking, your device rings. You glance at the screen and raise your hand, but your hovering fingers never pick it up.

steps.speaker: Chief
steps.content: Another unknown call? No, wait...
Shrooma seems to realize something. She stares intently at your hand, her gaze almost searing.
She leans forward, pupils shrunk... Beneath this aggressive look, you can sense a wavering fear. You know she's waiting for your "verdict."
The piercing ringtone never stops, tearing apart the thin trust recently established between you and Shrooma. The atmosphere has turned confrontational again.

steps.speaker: Chief
steps.content: ...Guess there's no other way.
In the tense air, your finger finally falls. You immediately hear the busy signal.

steps.speaker: Shrooma
steps.content: You hung up their call? What does this mean? Are you... going to side with me and help me skip the banquet?

steps.speaker: Chief
steps.content: Not really. I think we should attend it.
Before Shrooma shows any frustration or disappointment, you lay out the plan you've hastily put together.

steps.speaker: Chief
steps.content: But instead of bailing you out, we'll just apply for a leave. During this period, I will help conceal your identity as a Sinner.

steps.speaker: Chief
steps.content: I'll accompany you to the banquet as your instructor, and there I'll evaluate your family and social situation up close.

steps.speaker: Chief
steps.content: If your family can't positively influence your control over your emotions and power... As the Chief of the Bureau, I have the right to make the best managerial decision for my people.

steps.speaker: Chief
steps.content: Since you're not a little fool, you must understand what I mean, right?
Given Shrooma's precociousness, you're sure she understands your implication. But to your surprise, she doesn't seem as pleased and cooperative as you expected.
In her expression... you even see more painful hesitation than hopeful joy.

steps.speaker: Shrooma
steps.content: ...I see.
You take a mental note of this sophistication beyond her age, adding it to the list of mysteries about Shrooma you need to solve.
